 ORDER
Having regards to similitude in the controversy involved in these appeals they are heard analogously and are being decided by this common order.

2. These appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 have been preferred against the impugned award dated 27.02.2017 in Claim Case Nos.05/2017 (Amarsingh and others Vs.
Radheshyam and others), 06/2017 (Kailashchandra Vs. Radheshyam and others), 114/2014 (Amarjeet and others Vs. Radheshyam and others).

sentences.text: M.A.No.558/2017 has been filed by the survivors of deceased Naresh Kumar, M.A.No.561/2017 has been filed by injured Kailash Chandraand M.A.No.860/2017, M.A.No.862/2017 and M.A.No.864/2017 have been filed by the Insurance Company.

4. The claimants' case in nutshell is that on 13.09.2014 at about 2 P.M. the deceased Naresh was going on motorcycle CD Delux of his friend Jagdish Jatav along with deceased Rakesh and injured Kailash towards Gwaltoli.

Motorcycle was driven diligently on left side, suddenly respondent no.1 driving rashly and negligently tractor bearing No.MP-14-C-0608 with attached trolley bearing No.
MP-14-C-0611 came there and dashed the motorcycle and thereafter claimant Kailash Chandra who was standing with his motorcycle by the side was also dashed by the tractor trolley due to which he suffered fracture in his right thigh and also other grievous injuries all over body.

He was taken to The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Kailash Chandra on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182676623/
2 District hospital Neemuch.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Kailash Chandra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rakesh and Naresh succumbed to their injuries and passed away on the spot.
The incident was reported to the police station Neemch Cant on which Crime No.327/2014 for offence under Sections 297, 337 and 304-A was registered against the driver of the tractor.
He was arrested and tractor trolley was seized.

Thereafter, survivors of deceased Naresh and claimant/injured Kailash Chandra filed claim petitions for award of just and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3981 4 MA-558,561,860,862,864-2017 proper compensation.
The claim petitions were disposed of by impugned award dated 27.02.2017 which give rise to these miscellaneous appeals.
5. Counsel for the appellants/survivors of the deceased Naresh in M.A.No.558/2017 has submitted that the award passed by the Court below is on the lower side.

He further submits that the income of the deceased should have been taken at least as per circular issued by the Labour Department of the Government of M.P under the Minimum Wages Act prevailing on the date of incident and future prospects be also considered, as per the age of the deceased person.
The consortium amount should also have been awarded.
Accordingly, survivors of the deceased Naresh claim for enhancement of award amount and prays for dismissal of the appeals filed by the Insurance Company.

6. Counsel for the injured/appellant Kailash Chandra in M.A.No.561/2017 also urges the Court for enhancement of the award amount on similar grounds and prays for dismissal of the appeals filed by the Insurance Company.
7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the tractor bearing No.MP-14-C-0608 has been falsely implicated in this accident.
Death of Naresh who was sitting as pillion on the motorcycle of Jagdish Jatav has fell down from motorcycle, as Jagdish lost control on the motorcycle and collided with another motorcycle.
Jagdish Jatav has not been produced as NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3981 5 MA-558,561,860,862,864-2017 witness to the facts of the accident.
Contradictions appearing in the statement of Kailash Chandra have also not been considered.
The award has been passed against the settled principles of law.
The documentary and oral evidence have not been properly appreciated and the multiplier has also not been properly applied.
The compensation amount awarded to them is excessive.

On these submissions prays for allowing the appeals filed by the Insurance Company by exonerating the Insurance Company and dismissing the appeals filed by the survivors of the deceased Naresh and injured/claimant Kailash Chandra.

8. Heard and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

From perusal of the record it is apparent that FIR Ex.P-3 and Dehati Nalishi Ex.P-4 have been lodged in time and after investigation charge sheet has been filed against the respondent/driver Radheshyam who was driving the offending tractor trolley at the relevant point of time, when the accident took place.

No evidence has been given in rebuttal to the evidence adduced by the claimant Kailash Chandra and survivors of deceased Naresh therefore, the plea of Insurance Company that the offending tractor trolley has been falsely implicated in the case is not sustainable.

Learned Claims Tribunal has appreciated the evidence in this regard in right perspective and has given The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Kailash Chandra on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182676623/
3 affirmative finding on issue no.1 holding that the offending tractor trolley was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3981 6 MA-558,561,860,862,864-2017 driven rashly and negligently resulted in collision with the motorcycle whereon deceased Naresh was travelling with other deceased Rakesh and injured Kailash Chandra.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contributory negligence could not be established and negative finding has been given by the Claims Tribunal in this regard.
No breach has been found established, therefore, the Insurance Company has been held liable to pay compensation as awarded.
10. In M.A.No.558/2017 the deceased Naresh was aged about 20 years and was unmarried.

Since no positive evidence has been laid before the Claims Tribunal, therefore as per circular issued by the Labour Department of Government of M.P. under the Minimum Wages Act the income of unskilled labour comes to Rs.5,845/- which should have been considered, whereas Claims Tribunal has assessed the income as Rs.4,000/- per month which is on lower side without any basis.

entities.text: Labour Department of Government of M.P.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
In the head of future prospects 40% should be added in the income as per para 59.4 of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.
11.

sentences.text:
In view of the evidence available on record, in the factual matrix, this Court is of the view that the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced as under in M.A.No.558/2017 and M.A.No.561/2017:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3981 7 MA-558,561,860,862,864-2017 Rs.5,845/- + Rs.2,338/- (40% FP) =Rs.8,183/-
Loss of p.m. x 12 = Rs.98,196/- less 1/2 personal Dependency expenses =Rs.49,098/- x 18 (multiplier) = Rs.8,83,764/-
Funeral Rs.15,000/-
Expenses Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
Consortium Rs.40,000/- x 2=Rs.80,000/-
Total Amount Rs.9,93,764/-
MACT award Rs.4,57,000/-
Enhanced Rs.5,36,764/-
amount 12.

In M.A.No.561/2017 filed by appellant injured Kailash also, income of the injured is to be taken at par with the income of the deceased Naresh on the basis of circular under minimum wages Act issued by the Labour department of the Government of M.P.and permanent disability at 20% just The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Kailash Chandra on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182676623/
4 and proper compensation comes as under:-
Rs.5,845/- + Rs.2,338/- (40% FP) =Rs.8,183/- Permanent p.m. x 12 = Rs.98,196/- x 17 (multiplier) = disability Rs.16,69,332/- x 20% (PD)= Rs.3,33,866/- Medical Rs.69,800/-
expenses Total Rs.4,03,666/-
Amount MACT Rs.2,33,000/-
award Enhanced Rs.1,70,666/-
amount 13.

sentences.text: Accordingly, survivors of Naresh/claimants/appellants in (M.A.No.558/2017) are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.5,36,764/-over and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3981 8 MA-558,561,860,862,864-2017 above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The injured/claimant/appellant Kailash Chandra in (M.A.No.561/2017) is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,70,666/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

14. The appeal (M.A.No.558/2017) is valued as Rs.2,00,000/- and for the rest of the amount the claimants will pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days from today and only thereafter enhanced amount will be disbursed.
It is made clear, in case the court fees is not paid within the stipulated period, the appellants will not be entitled for claiming interest on the enhanced amount beyond 30 days' period.

15. Resultantly, the appeals (M.A.No.860/2017, 862/2017 and 864/2017) filed by the Insurance Company are dismissed and the appeals (M.A.No.558/2017) filed by the survivors of Naresh/claimants and (M.A.No.561/2017) filed by injured/claimant Kailash Chandra are allowed to the extent as indicated herein above.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
Let a copy of this order be kept in all connected matters.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE RJ The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Kailash Chandra on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182676623/
